cli.backup.long:
Saves a profile to the local repository: claude is Claude's data, projects is the working folders found in transcripts and your own folders. Without --profile every profile that is switched on runs; a profile that is switched off is not saved and an explicit request for it explains why. With --dry-run the files are read and nothing is stored.
Files another program holds are listed. Exit code 1 means something is missing from the snapshot.

cli.verify.long: Reads the file tree of the latest snapshot of a profile and compares it with the disk. Exit code 1 means something is missing or something banned got in.

cli.restore.long:
Brings back one session (--session), one project (--project) or everything (--all) from a copy. By default the files go to a new folder next to the local repository and nothing in place changes. With --apply the missing files are also put back where they were; a file that exists is never replaced. Without flags the command asks questions and shows the latest sessions.

On a new computer: backupclaude restore --repo <where the copy is> --all, then type the password from paper.
flag.restore.session: id of the session or its first characters (see list --sessions)
flag.restore.project: project: its folder name, a part of it or the full path
flag.restore.all: everything of the newest snapshots: Claude's data and the projects
flag.restore.from: copy to restore from: local or offsite
flag.restore.snapshot: snapshot id (see list --snapshots); the newest by default
flag.restore.to: folder to restore into; by default a new folder next to the local repository
flag.restore.apply: also put the missing files back in place; existing files are never replaced
flag.restore.dry_run: with --apply: show what would be put back and change nothing in place
flag.restore.map: OLD=NEW: move a folder of the old computer, for example D:\Work=E:\Work (may repeat)
flag.restore.repo: repository to restore from without settings: a folder or an rclone:/sftp: address
flag.restore.password_stdin: read the repository password from the first line of the input

cli.setup.long:
A short wizard. It checks the computer, installs restic and rclone, asks what to save (Claude's data only, or also the project folders), where to keep the local copy, whether to add an external copy and where to send failure messages, creates the password and the schedule, and takes the first snapshot.

Run it again at any time: it changes only what you answer and keeps the rest. With --yes it asks nothing.
cli.install.short: Copy the program into your folder and add it to the PATH
cli.install.long: Copies this program into the folder of the application and adds that folder to your PATH, so that the short command backupclaude works in any new terminal. Needs no administrator rights. The install command from the release page runs it.
cli.skill.long: The /backup skill lets you ask Claude Code to check the backups, list saved sessions and bring a lost session back. It calls this program with --json.
cli.skill.status.short: Say whether the /backup skill is installed
cli.update.long: Looks for a newer release, checks its SHA-256 against the published checksums and replaces the program. Settings, schedule and copies are not touched. A private repository needs a GitHub token in the BACKUPCLAUDE_GITHUB_TOKEN variable.
cli.uninstall.long: Removes the scheduled tasks and the programs (this one, restic and rclone), takes the program out of the PATH and removes the /backup skill. The copies and the password are never touched: the password stays in the system key store.
flag.setup.yes: do not ask: accept every default and the answers given in options
flag.setup.offsite: location of the external copy: rclone:remote:folder, sftp:user@host:/path or a folder

setup.paper.title: Write the password on paper
setup.paper.why: Your copies are encrypted. The password lives in the key store of this computer, and if the computer is lost, the copies cannot be opened without it.
setup.paper.step1: 1. Take a sheet of paper and a pen. Do not take a photo and do not save it in a file on this computer.
setup.paper.step2: 2. Copy the password exactly: 8 groups of 4 letters and digits. It has no O, I, L or U, so nothing can be mixed up with 0 or 1.
setup.paper.step3: 3. Read it back once, then keep the paper away from this computer: in a drawer at home or with your documents.
setup.paper.step4: 4. Without this password nobody can open your copies, including the author of the program.
setup.paper.command: To see the password, run this in your own terminal: backupclaude password --show
setup.paper.existing: The password already existed. If you have not written it on paper yet: backupclaude password --show
setup.q.show_password: Show the password now, to copy it onto paper?

cli.ui.long: Starts a small page on this computer and opens it in your browser: the state of the copies, the snapshots, restoring a session or a project, the settings. The page works only from this computer and only through the link printed here. When you close the page, the program ends: nothing stays running.
flag.ui.no_open: Do not open the browser, only print the link
ui.started:
The page is open in your browser: %s
Close the tab (or press Ctrl+C here) to finish.

Open this link in your browser: %s
The link works once. Close the tab (or press Ctrl+C here) to finish.
ui.open_failed: Could not open the browser. Open this link yourself: %s
ui.closed: The page is closed, the program has ended.
ui.listen_failed: Could not start the page on this computer
ui.listen_failed.hint: Try again; if it repeats, check that a firewall or security program does not block local connections of this program.

ui.denied.host.hint: Use the link from the window where you started the page.

ui.denied.origin.hint: Only the page itself may change anything.

cli.tray.long: Shows a small icon whose colour tells the state of the copies: green, yellow or red. Clicking it opens the page. It runs until you choose Quit in its menu. It is off by default; --enable makes it start when you log in, --disable stops that.

flag.tray.disable: Do not start the icon when you log in
tray.one_of.hint: Run the command again with one of the two.
tray.unsupported: The icon in the notification area works only on Windows for now
tray.unsupported.hint: Use the page instead: backupclaude ui
tray.already_running.hint: Look for it in the notification area, next to the clock. It may be under the arrow.

tray.autostart_failed.hint: The setting was not changed. Try again.

tray.start_failed.hint: Start it yourself with: backupclaude tray
tray.autostart_on: The icon will start when you log in. To show it now: backupclaude tray
tray.autostart_off: The icon will no longer start when you log in. One that is shown now stays until you choose Quit in its menu.
